text:
alex: noticing p99 tail latency spikes from shared-gpu pool s-pool-06 (us-east) over the last 12m, looks correlated with sustained KV cache growth from tenant:edge-ai (seen 3x spike in active KV entries)

ops-bot: ALERT: pool=s-pool-06 p99_latency=780ms (baseline ~48ms) kv_cache_mem_spill=true slab_frag=0.82

maria: oh dang, that's the same tenant we saw doing long multi-turn conversations yesterday. can we immediately divert their traffic to a dedicated slice or lower-priority lane?

shawn: before we move them, what's the capacity impact? do we have any warm dedicated capacity free in us-east that can take a steady 200 qps? moving will also increase $/token.

lee: quick mitigation we can roll: 1) enable routing override for tenant:edge-ai -> dedicated-slice-edge (if capacity) 2) else apply soft-throttle on prefix prefetching (limits KV growth)

lee: example command:
```
redwoodctl routing override set --tenant edge-ai --target dedicated-slice-edge --weight 1.0 --until 2026-04-01T12:00Z
```

maria: if dedicated not available, we should add policy: route-by-workload-size so huge-kv work lands on warm pools only. that's a config change but safer than evicting other customers.

shawn: cost estimate if we commit a small reserved slice for them for 24h: ~ $1.2k, vs repeated evictions causing 10-20% tail latency penalties across tenants which is worse for SLAs. I vote reserved short-term.

irina: I'll run a 5% canary for override now and watch p99 plus egress QPS. will post results in 10m. assigning SRE ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4987

irina: canary applied -> override to dedicated-slice-edge at 5% traffic

ops-bot: NOTE: canary route applied user=irina percent=5 target=dedicated-slice-edge

alex: thanks. also let's add a short-term KV eviction watermark on shared pools (like 75% mem used) to prevent slab fragmentation. that's a small runtime patch but buys time.

lee: ACK. I'll open a PR for runtime guard and throttle config: small change to router + cache manager. keeping defaults conservative.

maria: follow-up: postmortem draft should include model-size routing and tenant onboarding checklist (tell customers about KV-heavy workloads and recommend dedicated pools).

irina: monitoring so far: canary 5% -> p99 for s-pool-06 dropped from 780ms to 120ms; continuing to ramp to 25% if stable. will update INF-4987.

shawn: if ramp looks good, let's auto-scale a 2-GPU dedicated slice for 12h and invoice tenant for burst reserved capacity. ops, coordinate with finance.

alex: great work. summary: canary routing in progress, runtime KV guard PR from lee, INF-4987 tracks routing+billing follow-up. :thumbsup:
